extracted.intended_audience: petitioners, employers, immigration attorneys, and USCIS adjudicators handling P- and Q-classification petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements, definitions, evidentiary criteria, consultation, validity, extension, revocation, and procedural rules for USCIS petitions under P-1, P-2, P-3 (and related P-4/Q-1) nonimmigrant classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: petition, event, or performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an activity such as an athletic competition, athletic season, tournament, tour, exhibit, project, entertainment event, or engagement. Such activity could include short vacations, promotional appearances for the petitioning employer relating to the competition, event, or performance, and stopovers which are incidental and/or related to the activity. A group of related activities will also be considered an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For P-2 the event may be the duration of the reciprocal exchange agreement. For a P-1 athlete, the event may be the duration of the alien's contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the written agreement between the petitioner and the beneficiary(ies) that explains the terms and conditions of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contract shall describe the services to be performed, and specify the wages, hours of work, working conditions, and any fringe benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Culturally unique
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a style of artistic expression, methodology, or medium which is unique to a particular country, nation, society, class, ethnicity, religion, tribe, or other group of persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Essential support alien
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a highly skilled, essential person determined by the Director to be an integral part of the performance of a P-1, P-2, or P-3 alien because he or she performs support services which cannot be readily performed by a United States worker and which are essential to the successful performance of services by the P-1, P-2, alien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such alien must have appropriate qualifications to perform the services, critical knowledge of the specific services to be performed, and experience in providing such support to the P-1, P-2, or P-3 alien.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Group
rubrics_metrics.description: Means two or more persons established as one entity or unit to perform or to provide a service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Internationally recognized
rubrics_metrics.description: Means having a high level of achievement in a field evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition substantially above that ordinarily encountered, to the extent that such achievement is renowned, leading, or well-known in more than one country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Member of a group
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a person who is actually performing the entertainment services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an established organization in the United States which will not directly employ a P-1, P-2, or P-3 alien but will assume responsibility for the accuracy of the terms and conditions specified in the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Means two or more persons organized to perform together as a competitive unit in a competitive event.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-1 classification types and group membership thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: P-1 classification may be granted to an internationally recognized athlete individually or to a member of an entertainment group or athletic team that functions as a unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An entertainment group must have been established for a minimum of 1 year, and 75 percent of the members of the group must have been performing entertainment services for the group for a minimum of 1 year. A member may not perform services separate and apart from the entertainment group/team when relying on the group's recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-1 athlete: general criterion (international recognition and event requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A P-1 athlete must have an internationally recognized reputation as an international athlete or be a member of a foreign team that is internationally recognized. The athlete or team must be coming to the United States to participate in an athletic competition which has a distinguished reputation and which requires participation of an athlete or athletic team that has an international reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-1 athlete: evidentiary requirements (team or individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for an athletic team must be accompanied by evidence that the team as a unit has achieved international recognition. A petition for an athlete (individual or member of a U.S. team) must be accompanied by evidence that the athlete has achieved international recognition based on reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition for a P-1 athlete or athletic team shall include: (1) A tendered contract with a major United States sports league or team, or a tendered contract in an individual sport commensurate with international recognition, if such contracts are normally executed in the sport; AND (2) Documentation of at least two of the following: (i) participation to a significant extent in a prior season with a major U.S. sports league; (ii) participation in international competition with a national team; (iii) participation to a significant extent in a prior season for a U.S. college/university intercollegiate competition; (iv) written statement from governing body official detailing international recognition; (v) written statement from sports media member or recognized expert; (vi) evidence of international ranking, if applicable; (vii) evidence of significant honor or award.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-1 entertainment group: general criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: P-1 classification is accorded to an entertainment group to perform as a unit based on the international reputation of the group; individual entertainers shall not be accorded P-1 classification to perform separate and apart from the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided for special provisions, the group must have been internationally recognized as outstanding in the discipline for a sustained and substantial period; 75% of members must have a sustained and substantial relationship with the group for at least 1 year and provide functions integral to the group's performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-1 entertainment group: evidentiary criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for P-1 classification for members of an entertainment group shall be accompanied by evidence that the group has been established and performing regularly for at least 1 year, a statement listing members and exact employment dates, and evidence the group has been internationally recognized for a sustained and substantial period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International recognition may be demonstrated by nomination/receipt of significant international awards or by submitting three of the following types of documentation: (i) evidence of starring/leading performances in distinguished productions (reviews, ads, publicity, contracts, endorsements); (ii) reviews in major newspapers/trade journals/magazines; (iii) leading/starring services for distinguished organizations (articles/testimonials); (iv) record of major commercial or critically acclaimed successes (ratings, box office, sales reported in reputable sources); (v) recognition/testimonials from organizations, critics, government agencies, or recognized experts with clear indication of the author's authority; (vi) evidence of commanding a high salary or remuneration comparable to peers (contracts or reliable evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provisions and waivers for certain entertainment groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Director may waive certain requirements in special circumstances; circus personnel and some nationally known groups have exceptions to the 1-year and/or international recognition requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) Alien circus personnel are exempt from the 1-year membership and international recognition requirements if joining a circus nationally recognized as outstanding. (2) Director may waive international recognition for an entertainment group recognized nationally in consideration of special circumstances (media access, geography). (3) Director or Department of State may waive 1-year relationship in exigent circumstances (illness, substitution, augmentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: P-1 essential support: general and evidentiary criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An essential support alien may be granted P-1 classification based on a support relationship with a P-1 athlete, team, or entertainment group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition must be accompanied by: (1) a consultation from a labor organization with expertise in the alien's skill area; (2) a statement describing the alien's prior essentiality, critical skills, and experience with the principal alien(s); and (3) a copy of the written contract or a summary of the terms of the oral agreement between the alien(s) and the employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-2 classification: reciprocal exchange program requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: P-2 classification shall be accorded to artists or entertainers (individual or group) performing under a reciprocal exchange program between U.S. organization(s) and foreign organization(s) providing temporary exchange of artists/entertainers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange must be similar in caliber, terms/conditions (length, numbers), but this does not preclude individual or group exchange. Essential support persons may be accorded P-2 classification based on support relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-2 evidentiary requirements (reciprocal exchange)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for P-2 classification shall be accompanied by documentary proof related to the reciprocal exchange program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: (A) copy of the formal reciprocal exchange agreement between sponsoring U.S. organization(s) and foreign organization(s); (B) statement from sponsoring organization describing the reciprocal exchange relating to the petition; (C) evidence that an appropriate U.S. labor organization was involved in negotiating or has concurred with the exchange; (D) evidence that aliens and the U.S. artists subject to the exchange have comparable skills and similar terms/conditions of employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-2 essential support evidentiary criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An essential support alien may be granted P-2 classification based on support relationship with a P-2 entertainer or group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition for P-2 essential support personnel must be accompanied by: (1) consultation from a labor organization with expertise in the alien's skill; (2) a statement describing prior essentiality, critical skills, and experience with the principal alien(s); and (3) a copy of written contract or summary of oral agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-3 classification: culturally unique program general criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: P-3 classification may be accorded to artists or entertainers coming to the U.S. to develop, interpret, represent, coach, or teach a unique or traditional ethnic, folk, cultural, musical, theatrical, or artistic performance or presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The artist or entertainer must be coming to participate in cultural event(s) which will further understanding or development of his/her art form; program may be commercial or noncommercial.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-3 evidentiary criteria (culturally unique program)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for P-3 classification shall be accompanied by evidence demonstrating cultural uniqueness and authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable documentation includes: (A) affidavits/testimonials/letters from recognized experts attesting to authenticity and giving the expert's credentials and basis of knowledge; OR (B) documentation that the performance is culturally unique as evidenced by reviews in newspapers, journals, or other published materials; AND (C) evidence that all performances/presentations will be culturally unique events.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-3 essential support evidentiary criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An essential support alien may be granted P-3 classification based on support relationship with a P-3 entertainer or group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition for P-3 essential support personnel must include: (1) consultation from a labor organization with expertise in the skill area; (2) statement describing prior essentiality, critical skills, and experience with the principal alien(s); (3) copy of written contract or summary of oral agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory consultation with appropriate labor organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation with an appropriate labor organization regarding the nature of the work and the alien's qualifications is mandatory before a petition for P-1, P-2, or P-3 classification can be approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of consultation is generally a written advisory opinion signed by an authorized official and submitted with the petition. Consultations are advisory and not binding. If the advisory opinion is unfavorable it must set forth specific facts supporting the conclusion. Exceptions and expedited procedures (Service-initiated contact) and procedures when no appropriate labor organization exists are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation: expedited handling and Service-initiated requests
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where the Service determines a petition merits expeditious handling, the Service will contact the labor organization if no opinion is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The labor organization has 24 hours to respond to the Service's request; Service shall adjudicate after receipt of the response. The labor organization shall then furnish a written advisory opinion within 5 working days. If the labor organization fails to respond within 24 hours, the Service may render a decision without the advisory opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirements: P-1 athletes and entertainment groups (content of advisory opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For P-1 petitions, the labor organization should evaluate and/or describe the alien's or group's ability and achievements, comment on whether the alien/group is internationally recognized, and state whether the services to be performed are appropriate for an internationally recognized athlete or entertainment group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A labor organization may submit a letter of no objection in lieu of a full advisory opinion if it has no objection to approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirements: P-1 circus personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory opinion should comment on whether the circus which will employ the alien has national recognition and any other aspect of the beneficiary's qualifications deemed appropriate by the labor organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If opinion is unfavorable it must set forth specific supporting facts; a letter of no objection is an alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirements: P-2 reciprocal exchange program
rubrics_metrics.description: For P-2 petitions under a reciprocal exchange program, the labor organization's advisory opinion must verify the existence of a viable exchange program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opinion shall comment on the bona fides of the reciprocal exchange and specify whether the exchange meets the regulatory requirements for P-2 classification; an unfavorable opinion must include specific facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirements: P-3 culturally unique program
rubrics_metrics.description: For P-3 petitions, consultation with an appropriate labor organization is required to evaluate cultural uniqueness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If favorable, the opinion should evaluate cultural uniqueness of the alien's skills, state whether events are cultural in nature, and whether the event/activity is appropriate for P-3 classification. An unfavorable opinion must set forth specific facts. Letter of no objection is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirements: essential support aliens (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written consultation on petitions for essential support aliens must be with a labor organization with expertise in the skill area involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If favorable, the advisory opinion must evaluate the alien's essentiality to and working relationship with the artist/entertainer, and state whether U.S. workers are available to perform the support services. An unfavorable opinion must set forth specific facts; letter of no objection is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor organizations list and absence of appropriate labor organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service shall list in its Operations Instructions those organizations which have agreed to provide advisory opinions and those occupations/fields where no appropriate labor organization exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is not exclusive or exhaustive; Service and petitioners may use other sources to identify appropriate labor organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of petition: adjudicator's consideration and Form I-797 notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall consider all the evidence submitted and such other evidence as he or she may independently require. The Director shall notify the petitioner of approval on Form I-797, which includes the beneficiary's name, classification, and the petition's period of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording petition validity: start and end date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new P petition is approved before the requested services begin, the approved petition shall show the actual dates requested by the petitioner as the validity period (subject to regulatory limits). If approved after services began, the approved petition will generally show a validity period commencing with the date of approval and ending with the date requested by the petitioner (subject to limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested period exceeds regulatory limits, petition approved only up to the specified limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity limits by P classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval periods for P petitions must conform to regulatory limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P-1 individual athlete: up to 5 years. P-1 athletic team: period determined to complete competition/event, not to exceed 1 year. P-1 entertainment group: period determined necessary to complete performance/event, not to exceed 1 year. P-2 and P-3: period necessary to complete the event/activity, not to exceed 1 year. Spouse and unmarried minor children receive P-4 status subject to same period and limitations; they may not accept employment unless granted employment authorization. Essential support aliens' petitions valid for period necessary to complete event, not to exceed 1 year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of denial and appellate rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall be notified of the decision, the reasons for the denial, and the right to appeal the denial under 8 CFR part 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no appeal from a decision to deny an extension of stay to the alien or a change of nonimmigrant status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation: petitioner duties and Director authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must immediately notify the Service of any changes in terms/conditions of employment which may affect eligibility; file amended petition if continuing to employ; if no longer employing, send explanatory letter. The Director may revoke a petition at any time, even after expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic revocation triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of an unexpired petition is automatically revoked if the petitioner (or employer in agent-filed petition) goes out of business, files a written withdrawal, or notifies the Service that the beneficiary is no longer employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic revocations may not be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation on notice: grounds and rebuttal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall send notice of intent to revoke if he/she finds that: (1) beneficiary no longer employed in capacity specified; (2) statement of facts in petition not true and correct; (3) petitioner violated terms/conditions of approved petition; (4) petitioner violated regulatory requirements; or (5) approval violated regulation or involved gross error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of intent to revoke shall contain detailed grounds and time period allowed for petitioner's rebuttal. Petitioner may submit evidence in rebuttal within 30 days. Director will consider all relevant evidence before revoking. Revocation on notice may be appealed under 8 CFR part 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission period and pre-/post-arrival grace
rubrics_metrics.description: A beneficiary may be admitted to the United States for the petition's validity period plus up to 10 days before the validity period begins and 10 days after the validity period ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The beneficiary may not work except during the validity period of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of petition validity (filing requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must file a request to extend the validity of the original petition on the form prescribed by USCIS to continue or complete the same activity or event specified in the original petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition extension generally may be filed only if the validity of the original petition has not expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay: procedure and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: To extend the alien's stay to continue or complete the same event/activity, the petitioner shall file the prescribed USCIS form accompanied by a statement explaining reasons for extension; the petitioner must also request a petition extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The beneficiary must be physically present in the U.S. when the extension of stay is filed. The Director makes separate determinations on petition extension and extension of stay. If the alien leaves while extension is pending, petitioner may request the Director to cable notification of approval to the consular office abroad where alien will apply for a visa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension periods by classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized extension periods depend on classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P-1 individual athlete and essential support personnel: extension up to 5 years for a total period of stay not to exceed 10 years. Other P-1 teams, entertainment groups, P-2, and P-3 aliens and their essential support personnel: extensions may be authorized in increments of 1 year to continue or complete the same event/activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of permanent labor certification or preference petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of a permanent labor certification or the filing of a preference petition for an alien shall not be a basis for denying a P petition, a request to extend such a petition, or the alien's admission, change of status, or extension of stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision does not include essential support personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a strike at the place of employment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Secretary of Labor certifies a strike or labor dispute involving a work stoppage at the place where beneficiary is to be employed and employment would adversely affect U.S. workers' wages/conditions, a P petition shall be denied or an approved petition (if alien not yet entered or not commenced employment) automatically suspended and application for admission denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If strike not certified, Commissioner shall not deny or suspend. If alien already commenced employment and is participating in a strike/work stoppage, participation alone shall not constitute failure to maintain status solely on account of the strike, but status and authorized stay are not modified or extended. Violations of status or overstaying remain subject to deportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form I-797 (approval notice utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service shall notify the petitioner on Form I-797 whenever a visa petition or an extension is approved under P classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A beneficiary who does not require a visa may present a copy of the approved notice at a Port-of-Entry to facilitate entry. A beneficiary who requires a visa and whose visa expired before intended return may use Form I-797 to apply for a new or revalidated visa during the petition's validity. The copy of Form I-797 shall be retained by the beneficiary and presented during the validity of the petition when reentering the U.S. to resume the same employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return transportation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an alien who entered under P classification has employment terminate for reasons other than voluntary resignation, the employer whose offer formed the basis of status and the petitioner are jointly and severally liable for the reasonable cost of return transportation of the alien abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this paragraph, 'abroad' means the alien's last place of residence prior to entry into the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-1 international cultural exchange visitor: program admission and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonimmigrant may be authorized to enter as a participant in an approved international cultural exchange program (Q-1) for the purpose of providing practical training, employment, and sharing the history, culture, and traditions of the country of the alien's nationality; admission period is the duration of the approved program or 15 months, whichever is shorter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Q-1 alien shall not be readmitted in Q-1 status unless the alien has resided and been physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior year; brief trips to the U.S. for pleasure or business during that year do not break continuity of the one-year foreign residency requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q-1 program approval: petitioner and qualified employer definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. employer shall petition the Attorney General on the form prescribed by USCIS for approval of an international cultural exchange program designed to provide opportunity for the American public to learn about foreign cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided include 'country of nationality', 'doing business' (regular, systematic, continuous provision of goods/services by a qualified employer that has employees), 'duration of program' (not to exceed 15 months), 'international cultural exchange visitor' (residence abroad with no intent to abandon and coming temporarily to participate in an approved program), 'petitioner' (employer or designated agent employed on a permanent basis in executive/managerial capacity, with agent being U.S. citizen, LPR, or certain temporary status aliens), and 'qualified employer' (U.S. or foreign legal entity that administers an approved program).
